slides.say: For every number x that's not zero, diamond of x is three over x. Which of the following must be true for all positive a and b?
A hard one. Must be true, so we try to break each choice. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, technically, and then by understanding.

[short pause] Let's start technically. Choice number one, three over a is smaller than three. a is positive, so multiply by a with no flip, and divide by three. One is smaller than a. True only when a is above one, and a could be one half, then three over a is six. Out.
at: Choice number one, three over a

slides.say: Choice number three, three over a divided by three over b. Multiply by the reciprocal, b over a, not a over b. Out.

Choice number four, three over a smaller than three over a plus one. Both are positive, so cross-multiply with no flip and divide by three. a plus one smaller than a, so one smaller than zero. Never true. Out.
Choice number two, three over a, times a. The a cancels, three. And three over b times b, three too. Three equals three for every a and b. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way. What's different? We read what the diamond does, instead of moving terms. Choice number one. For a above one it's true, two gives three halves, three gives one. But a equal to one gives three, and one half gives six.

Choice number three. Three over x is three times x to the negative one, and a minus power means flip. So b over a. Choice number four. A bigger denominator makes a smaller fraction. a is two, three halves is not smaller than one.
Choice number two. Three over a is three times the reciprocal of a, and a number times its reciprocal is one. So three, every time. Choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: three, every time. Choice number two
